            💀
            Dangerous Endpoints
            0
            CRITICAL
            ▾
          

          

            
Endpoints dangerous by design — arbitrary code/SQL execution, admin/IAM privilege escalation, destructive bulk mutation, deserialization or debug surfaces. Naming-pattern heuristic — verify each one manually before reporting as exploited. Click a row for the full write-up (impact, CWE/OWASP, suggested CVSS, recommendation).

            

              
#EndpointCategoryMatched KeywordsAuthSeverityCVSS

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🕵️
            Sensitive Data Exposure
            0
            HIGH
            ▾
          

          

            
OWASP API3:2023 — 2xx response schemas with high-signal sensitive fields (password, accessToken, SSN, credit card…). Bare token/secret/pin skipped to cut FPs. A lead, not proof the field is populated at runtime.

            

              
#EndpointSensitive FieldsSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            ✍️
            Mass Assignment Risk
            0
            HIGH
            ▾
          

          

            
OWASP API6:2023 — POST/PUT/PATCH bodies accepting high-signal privilege fields (isAdmin, superuser, ownerId, balance…) or open additionalProperties. Common fields like permissions/status/role are ignored to cut FPs.

            

              
#EndpointWritable Privileged FieldsSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🔑
            Leaked Secrets in Spec Examples
            0
            CRITICAL
            ▾
          

          

            
Hardcoded credentials/tokens accidentally left in example/default values — a surprisingly common find in harvested or dev-portal specs.

            

              
#TypeLocationValue (truncated)Severity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🌐
            Insecure Servers (http://)
            0
            HIGH
            ▸
          

          

            
Server URLs using plaintext HTTP — credentials/tokens travel unencrypted.

            

              
#Server URLSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🗝️
            Weak apiKey Placement
            0
            MEDIUM
            ▸
          

          

            
apiKey auth carried in the query string or a cookie instead of a header — leaks into server/proxy access logs, browser history and Referer headers.

            

              
#SchemeSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            📡
            GET With Request Body
            0
            MEDIUM
            ▸
          

          

            
GET operations that declare a requestBody — non-standard, and often hides a real side effect behind a "safe" verb.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🧟
            Deprecated Endpoints (still live)
            0
            LOW
            ▸
          

          

            
Marked deprecated: true in the spec but still routable — classic "zombie API" inventory risk.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🔓
            Unsecured Endpoints
            0
            CRITICAL
            ▾
          

          

            
Endpoints with no security definition and not covered by a global policy. Health/login/oauth/docs are allowlisted by default (see Expected Public).

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🌐
            Expected Public Endpoints
            0
            INFO
            ▸
          

          

            
Unauthenticated but allowlisted as intentional public surfaces (health, login, oauth, swagger docs…). Not counted as Unsecured. Enable “Strict unsecured” on upload to disable this filter.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            📡
            Live Probe Results
            0
            INFO
            ▸
          

          

            
Optional safe probes against Unsecured + Dangerous endpoints. Mutating methods use OPTIONS only — never sends destructive bodies.

            

              
#EndpointProbeStatusVerdict

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🔁
            Duplicate Endpoints
            0
            WARNING
            ▸
          

          

            
Same METHOD + path defined more than once in the spec. Spec-style lint — not a runtime vuln.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🔀
            Multiple Methods on Same Path
            0
            INFO
            ▸
          

          

            
Normal REST often exposes GET+POST on one path. Treated as lint inventory — hidden by default via “Hide lint noise”.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🔗
            Broken $refs
            0
            HIGH
            ▾
          

          

            
Local $refs pointing to undefined components (parameters, schemas, requestBodies, responses, headers, path-level params, …).

            

              
#LocationSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            📎
            External $refs (unresolved)
            0
            INFO
            ▸
          

          

            
Non-local $refs (other files/URLs). Not fetched during this static scan — verify manually if needed.

            

              
#LocationSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            📭
            Missing Response Definitions
            0
            MEDIUM
            ▸
          

          

            
Spec-style lint — no responses block. Hidden by default via “Hide lint noise”.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            🏷️
            Missing operationId
            0
            LOW
            ▸
          

          

            
Spec-style lint — missing operationId. Hidden by default via “Hide lint noise”.

            

              
#EndpointSeverity

              
            

          

        


        
        

          

            📋
            All Unique Endpoints

            INFO
            ▸
          

          

            
Complete list of all unique endpoints discovered in the spec.

Intruder attack types

          
The difference is how many positions you mark and how payload sets iterate across them.

        

        
      

      

        

          
Sniper

          
N lists · 1 position at a time

          
Each list position has its own payloads. Positions marked Unique format are skipped by the attack and get a fresh value on every hit.

          
Best: different fuzz per param (id vs header vs body)

        

        

          
Battering ram

          
1 list · same value everywhere

          
Puts the same payload into all positions at once.

          
Best: same value in user+pass / CSRF pairs

        

        

          
Pitchfork

          
N lists · line-by-line pairs

          
Position 1 ← List A line i, Position 2 ← List B line i. Stops at the shortest list.

          
Best: known pairs (userId + token)

        

        

          
Cluster bomb

          
N lists · all combinations

          
Tries every combination: |A| × |B| × … requests.

          
Best: multi-param fuzz / path × method

        

      

      

        Example — Position lists 5 and 4 (2 marks): 
        Sniper 9 (5+4) · Ram 5 (shared list) · Pitchfork 4 · Cluster 20

          🔓 Offline HMAC Secret Dictionary Cracker
        

        
          Alg: (No Token)
        
      

      

        If your API uses symmetric HMAC algorithms (HS256, HS384, HS512), developers often set weak, default, or leaked keys (like secret, jwt_secret, or company name). ⚡🔐

      
API Sentinel

      
Version 1.3.0

      
Focused tools for testing REST APIs, built around one shared workflow — capture a request, then put it under pressure. Below is what each one actually does.

    


    

      
✨

      

        
What's New in 1.3.0

        
    
          
  • Unique format + unique list together — keep a format such as {uuid} on other fields while a CSV/XLSX list (or dataset case) still drives the field you are testing.
    • 
          
  • Unique lists (CSV / XLSX) — import a column of values in API Validator and in Runner Random. First row is the param name.
    • 
          
  • List consume rules — 2xx uses the next row, 4xx/5xx retries the same value, 409/422 “already exists” skips that row, and an empty list stops the run with a popup.
    • 
          
  • List wins on the bound path — if a unique list is mapped to a param, that list is used instead of the unique format for that field.
    • 
          
  • Nested JSON unique values — unique formats and lists apply inside nested objects and arrays, not only top-level fields.
    • 
          
  • case misconfig tag — 409/422 responses that say the value already exists (for example ALREADY_EXISTS) get a yellow tag. Pass/fail scoring stays the same.
    • 
          
  • Collection export / Runner import — unique formats, unique lists, and dataset case ids travel with the AV collection so Runner can replay the same setup.
    • 
          
  • Full request / response — Runner, Collection Runner, and HTML report show the full body and cURL, with search and Copy body.
    • 
          
  • HTML Failed cases — the exported Dashboard report shows the case misconfig pill next to the case name, without overlapping text.
    • 
          
  • CSV header matching — headers like fieldDetails[0].name match params written as fieldDetails.0.name.
    • 
          
  • Alert popups — long import errors wrap and scroll so long param paths stay readable.
    • 
        

      

    


    

      
⚡

      

        
API Validator Pro

        
Captures live XHR/Fetch traffic straight from the browser — or imports a HAR file or cURL command — and fires hundreds of positive and negative test cases against every parameter automatically. Results land in a live pass/fail table with the full request and response bodies, exportable as CSV or HTML.

      

    


    

      
🔐

      

        
Auth Validator Pro

        
Replays a captured request with a valid Bearer token, an invalid or empty one, or both — to confirm an endpoint actually enforces authentication instead of quietly letting unauthenticated calls through.

      

    


    

      
🌐

      

        
APISphere

        
A built-in Postman-style REST client — collections, environment-style variables, collection-level auth, and a Collection Runner that replays a whole collection with a CSV or JSON data file feeding values into every iteration. Collections export and import as plain JSON.

      

    


    

      
🔀

      

        
Method Tampering

        
Probes whether an endpoint quietly accepts HTTP methods it was never meant to — sending GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and more across the same path to surface verbs the server shouldn't be honoring.

      

    


    

      
🗑️

      

        
Soft Delete

        
Checks whether records marked as "deleted" are actually gone, or still reachable through the API — a common gap where the UI hides data the backend is still happy to serve.

      

    


    

      
🔍

      

        
IDOR Tester

        
Finds weak, ID-based endpoints and replays them as a second user to check whether one account can read or modify another account's data — the classic Insecure Direct Object Reference check.

      

    


    

      
🎯

      

        
Params Tamper

        
Mutates query, body, and header values with boundary, type-confusion, and malformed inputs to find the spots where input validation quietly falls apart.

      

    


    

      
📄

      

        
Swagger Scan

        
An OpenAPI spec auditor — it reads the spec itself looking for unsecured endpoints, duplicate definitions, broken $refs, and paths that expose more HTTP methods than they should.

      

    


    

      
🔒

      

        
RSQL Tester

        
Targets RSQL/filter-style query parameters, body fields, and custom headers with crafted payloads to catch RSQL injection vulnerabilities in search and filter endpoints.

      

    


    

      
🛡️

      

        
API Scan

        
A broader, all-in-one active security scanner that runs as a background job and reports progress as it goes — a fast sweep across many checks at once instead of running each tool one by one.

      

    


    

      
📤

      

        
File Upload

        
Parses a captured multipart upload and replays it with a battery of malicious files — bad extensions, MIME mismatches, path traversal, null bytes, EXIF/SVG/HTML polyglots — to catch unrestricted file upload issues.

      

    


    

      
🎯

      

        
XSS Test

        
Takes a captured cURL command, discovers its parameters automatically, and fires a set of XSS payloads at each one — reporting exactly where and how the response reflects them back unescaped.

      

    


    

      
🧬

      

        
JS & Secret Analyser

        
Advanced credential & secret scanner with official TruffleHog detectors (800+ active formats with live verification), native Shannon Entropy engine, Swagger/OpenAPI spec auditing, and live response replay scanning. Uncovers cloud keys, AI tokens, private keys, database strings, and sensitive PII.

      

    


    

      
🛡️

      

        
LLM/Command Injection

        
Scores parameters for OS-command reachability, then runs tiered command-injection and LLM prompt-injection / jailbreak payloads — with canary confirmation, optional OOB callbacks, and a live findings table.

      

    


    

      
💥

      

        
Intruder

        
Burp-style Sniper: Import cURL, mark §payload positions§, generate or paste payloads, fire Sniper, then review requests on Scanning and graphs on Dashboard.

      

    


    

      
⚡

      

        
API Fuzzer

        
High-performance parameter fuzzing engine with integrated Arjun hidden parameter discovery. Discovers undocumented GET, POST, and JSON parameters using differential response analysis, then executes boundary mutation payloads, rate-limited fuzzing, and WAF evasion routines.

      

    


    

      
🔬

      

        
Nuclei Scanner

        
Template-powered vulnerability scanner leveraging ProjectDiscovery Nuclei v3. Executes curated CVE, security misconfiguration, and exposure templates across APIs, HAR captures, and Swagger specs with live severity triage and detailed vulnerability reports.

      

    


    

      
🔑

      

        
JWT Tool

        
Comprehensive JSON Web Token security suite addressing OWASP API1 & API2 vulnerabilities. Features real-time token decoding, claims tampering, signature bypass ('none' algorithm & HMAC/RSA key confusion / CVE-2015-9235), dictionary-based secret cracking, and live replay validation.

      

    


    

      
🌐

      

        
Nikto Scanner

        
Industry-standard web server & API security auditing engine. Tests for over 7,000 potentially dangerous files and programs, outdated server versions, missing security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options), dangerous HTTP methods, and server misconfigurations.

      

    


    

      
Designed & Developed by VW Security Team

      
Contributors: Ajay, Hemant, Himanshu

      
Version: 1.3.0
